PR Summary by Qodo

Merge main into release/3.2 and resolve Guard conflicts 🐞 Bug fix ✨ Enhancement 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation ⚙️ Configuration changes 🕐 40+ Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Merges current main into release/3.2 while retaining non-conflicting release work.
>• Resolves overlapping Guard hunks in favor of main’s native authority behavior.
>• Carries forward expanded runtime, dashboard, extension, release, and security coverage.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD H["Harness hooks"] --> A["Python adapters"] --> D["Guard daemon"] --> R["Rust authority"] --> P["Policy snapshots"] --> E["Decision evidence"] D --> U["Dashboard controls"] C["CI and release"] --> D C --> R C --> U ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Rebase release/3.2 onto main
- ➕ Produces linear history. - ➕ Makes individual conflict resolutions visible per replayed commit. - ➖ Rewrites the shared release branch. - ➖ Requires repeatedly resolving conflicts across release commits. - ➖ Raises coordination risk for existing release work.
2. Cherry-pick selected main changes
- ➕ Limits the release branch to explicitly selected changes. - ➕ Can reduce unrelated release surface area. - ➖ Risks omitting transitive runtime, contract, or test dependencies. - ➖ Creates duplicate commit identities and future merge conflicts. - ➖ Is impractical for this highly interconnected change set.
>**Recommendation:** Keep the merge-based approach. It preserves release history and imports the complete dependency graph from main; review should concentrate on overlapping conflict hunks, native-policy readiness, deadline propagation, inactive-app passthrough, MFA-protected disconnects, and green release/CI evidence.

✅ 3 closed
✅ Bug: Extracted mixin methods over-indented, breaking module import > 📄 src/codex_plugin_scanner/guard/daemon/runtime_hook_evidence_writer_journal.py:55-69 📄 src/codex_plugin_scanner/guard/native_policy_snapshot_resident_inputs.py:11-25 > In both new files the class body opens with statements at 4-space indent (docstring, and `guard_home: Path` in the resident mixin), but every method that follows is indented at 8 spaces with no compound statement opening a new block. Python raises `IndentationError: unexpected indent` at the first `def`, so neither module can be parsed or imported. `runtime_hook_evidence_writer.py` imports `RuntimeHookEvidenceWriterJournalMixin`/`RuntimeHookEvidenceWriterStats`/`persist_native_decision_receipt` from the journal module and `native_policy_snapshot_publisher_inputs.py` imports `NativePolicySnapshotResidentInputsMixin`, so both consumers crash on import as well. Dedent every method (and its body) in each mixin class by 4 spaces so method `def`s align at 4 spaces with the class docstring.
✅ Bug: Literal in argparse line breaks module parse > 📄 scripts/profile_guard_mcp_streaming_session.py:85 > Line 85 of profile_guard_mcp_streaming_session.py physically contains a literal backslash-n (`store_true") > parser.add_argument`) rather than a real line break. A backslash outside a string that is not immediately followed by a newline is a `SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character`, so the entire module fails to parse and cannot be imported or executed at all. Split the statement onto two physical lines.
✅ Bug: Streaming session runs owned variant, not streaming > 📄 scripts/profile_guard_mcp_streaming_session.py:59-60 📄 scripts/profile_guard_mcp_streaming_session.py:25 > In profile_guard_mcp_streaming_session.py, run_case forwards preparation_variant="owned" (and passes streaming_preparation_pilot as preparation_pilot). run_case_common then stores the pilot flag under the `owned_preparation_pilot` spec key and spawns the worker with `--variant owned`, so the streaming adapter branch in profile_guard_mcp_worker.py (guard_mcp_streaming_preparation_pilot, loaded_adapter_sha256, _binding_matches wrap) is never exercised. The local _worker helper here correctly uses "streaming", making the mismatch clear. The script therefore silently measures the owned candidate while claiming to profile "explicit streaming candidate F".
